q: 1. With the moisture content of 5 to 10% by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by
explain: At moisture contents in the 5-10% range, sand bulking reaches values on the order of 50% increase in volume as per standard bulking curves.

q: 2. The main requirement, which a ware-house should fulfill is that
options: its walls should be water proof masonry construction
it must have large number of windows
explain: A cement warehouse must protect stored cement from moisture, requiring both water-proof walls and a leak-proof roof (options a and b together).

q: 3. The term 'ware-house pack' means
options: pressure compaction of bags in lower layers
pressure exertion of bags on upper layers
explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the phenomenon where cement bags stored in lower layers get compacted due to the pressure of bags stacked above them.

q: 4. According to IS: 382-1963, a good aggregate should be
explain: As per IS: 382-1963, aggregates for concrete must be chemically inert, sufficiently strong, and hard and durable, satisfying all listed conditions.

q: 5. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, high alumina cement has
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial setting time and final setting time
lower initial setting time and final setting time
explain: High alumina cement is characterized by a longer initial setting time but a comparatively shorter final setting time than OPC, giving rapid strength gain once setting begins.

q: 6. In designing a ware-house, it is assumed that
options: each bag contains 50 kg of cement
floor area occupied by one bag of cement is 0.3 m2
height of each cement bag containing 35 liters of cement is 0.18 m
explain: Standard warehouse design assumptions include a 50kg bag weight, about 0.3m² floor area per bag, and about 0.18m height per bag containing roughly 35 liters, so all these hold together.

q: 7. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
explain: Aggregate larger than 75 mm in size is termed cyclopean aggregate, generally used in mass concrete works like dams.

q: 8. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the maximum size of a coarse aggregate, is 75mm and minimum 4.75mm
the maximum size of a fine aggregate, is 4.75mm and minimum 0.075mm
the material having particles of size varying from 0.06mm to 0.002mm is known as slit
the material having particles of size less than 0.002mm, is known as clay
explain: All the given size classifications for coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, silt, and clay are correct according to standard particle size definitions.

q: 9. In order to obtain the best workability of concrete, the preferred shape of aggregate is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and least interlocking/friction, which gives the best workability for a given water-cement ratio.

q: 10. Bulking of sand is maximum if moisture content is about
explain: The bulking effect in sand is typically at its peak (maximum volume increase) at around 4% moisture content, before it decreases again as the sand becomes saturated.

q: 11. In Q. No. 70 the aggregates will be known as elongated aggregate if its length is not less than
explain: Elongated if length ≥ 1.8 × mean size = 1.8 × 67.5 = 121.5mm (using the thrice-mean-size type criterion referenced in these questions).

q: 12. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
explain: By definition, an aggregate is classified as flaky when its least dimension (thickness) is less than 3/5th (0.6 times) of its mean dimension.

q: 13. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
options: four times than the mean size
explain: A flaky aggregate is further classified as elongated when its length exceeds thrice the mean size of the particle.

q: 14. The minimum percentage of void in round aggregate is
explain: Round/spherical aggregates, being able to pack closely, exhibit a minimum void percentage of about 33% compared to irregular or angular shapes.

q: 15. The fineness modulus of fine aggregate is in the range of
explain: Fine aggregate (sand) typically has a fineness modulus in the range of about 2.0 to 3.5, differentiating it from coarse aggregate which has a much higher FM.

q: 16. The light weight aggregates may be obtained from
explain: Lightweight aggregates such as pumice and scoria are derived from volcanic sources, which contain porous, low-density material.

q: 17. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: sands obtained from pits, is washed to remove clay and silt
sands obtained from flooded pits, need not be washed before use
sea shore sands contain chloride which cause efflorescence
the chloride in sea shore sand and shingle may cause corrosion of reinforcement if the concrete is porous
explain: All statements about pit sand washing, flooded pit sand, and sea shore sand chloride effects (efflorescence, corrosion) are correct.

q: 18. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: sand stones may be defined into calcareous, siliceous and ferruginous sand stones
concrete using sand stones, cracks due to excessive shrinkage
very hard and close grained crystallized lime stones are suitable aggregates but provide low strength
broken bricks produce a concrete having good fire resisting qualities
explain: All the statements regarding sand stone types, shrinkage cracking, limestone strength, and broken brick fire resistance are correct.

q: 19. The construction joints in cement concrete
options: should be located where bending moment is large
should be located where shear force is large
should not be provided at the corners
should be spaced at a distance of 3 m part in case of huge structures
explain: Construction joints should be avoided at corners since these are critical stress concentration zones and joints there could weaken structural integrity.

q: 20. The bulk density of an aggregate does not depend upon
options: size and shape of the container
explain: Bulk density is a material property depending on aggregate size, shape, specific gravity, and grading — it does not depend on the size and shape of the measuring container.

q: 21. The most useless aggregate is, whose surface texture is
explain: A glossy surface texture prevents good bonding between the aggregate and the cement paste, making it the least useful/desirable aggregate surface type.

q: 22. The aggregate impact value of the aggregate used in
options: road pavement concrete is less than 30
explain: As per IS specifications, the aggregate impact value limits given for building concrete (<45), road pavement (<30), and runway concrete (<30) are all correct.

q: 23. The creep strains are
options: caused due to dead loads only
caused due to live loads only
explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation of concrete under sustained/continued stress, which can result from both dead and live loads acting over time.

q: 24. The bulk density of aggregates depends upon its
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced together by particle shape, grading (size distribution), and the degree of compaction achieved during placement.

q: 25. The void ratio of
options: single size coarse aggregate is roughly 0.45
explain: The void ratios given for single size coarse aggregate, graded coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate are all approximately correct as standard values.

q: 26. The effect of creep on modular ratio is
options: either to decrease or to increase it
explain: Creep effectively reduces the modulus of elasticity of concrete over time, which increases the modular ratio (Es/Ec) used in design.

q: 27. The aggregate containing moisture in pores and having its surface dry, is known as
explain: Saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate is defined as aggregate whose pores are filled with moisture but whose surface is dry, neither absorbing nor contributing extra water to the mix.

q: 28. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: bulking of sand is caused due to formation of a thin film of surface moisture
fine sand bulks more than coarse sand
with 10% moisture content by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by 50%
the volume of fully saturated sand, is equal to the volume of dry and loose sand
explain: All statements regarding causes of bulking, fine sand bulking more, the 10% moisture bulking figure, and saturated sand volume equaling dry sand volume are correct.

q: 29. For a structure subjected to sea water, the cement used is
explain: High alumina cement offers strong resistance to sulphate and chemical attack found in sea water environments, making it a preferred choice for marine structures per this text.

q: 30. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the bulk density of fine aggregate is usually about 10 percent more than that of coarse aggregate of similar composition
the specific gravity of aggregate is important for the determination of the moisture content
the absorption and porosity of an aggregate, influence the property of the concrete
a highly absorptive aggregate reduces the workability of concrete considerably
explain: All statements about bulk density comparison, specific gravity's role, and absorption/porosity effects on concrete workability are correct.

q: 31. If 20 kg of a coarse aggregate is sieved through 80mm, 40 mm, 20 mm, 10 mm, 4.75 mm, 2.36 mm, 1.18 mm, 600 micron, 300 micron and 150 micron standard sieves and the weights retained are 0 kg, 2 kg, 5 kg, 6 kg, 4 kg, 3kg respectively, the fineness modulus of the aggregate, is
explain: Fineness modulus = sum of cumulative percentage retained on standard sieves ÷ 100. Calculating cumulative % retained (0,10,35,65,85,100 for 6 sieves shown, remaining sieves 100 each for 4 finer sieves) gives a total of 740/100 = 7.40.

q: 32. The approx. ratio of the strength of the cement conc. of 7 days to that of 28 days is
explain: Concrete typically develops about 65% of its 28-day strength by 7 days of curing, giving an approximate ratio of 0.65.

q: 33. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregates F.M 5.4 in
explain: Using the mixture rule: % of fine aggregate = (6.8-5.4)/(6.8-2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, closest standard answer given as 50% per the answer key provided.

q: 34. IS sieve No. 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: IS sieves of 10 mm and 4.75 mm size are commonly used to determine and control the grading of fine aggregate (sand).

q: 35. The approx. ratio of direct tensile strength to flexural strength is
explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is approximately half (0.5) of its flexural strength (modulus of rupture), since flexural tests measure extreme fiber stress differently from direct tension.

q: 36. If a grading curve is horizontal between the portions of 20 mm IS sieve and 4.75 mm IS sieve, graded aggregates do not contain.
explain: A horizontal segment on the grading curve between 20mm and 4.75mm sieve indicates a gap grading, meaning particles of 20mm, 10mm, and 4.75mm intermediate sizes are all absent.

q: 37. For the construction of cement concrete floor, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates, is
explain: For thin sections like concrete floors, a smaller maximum aggregate size of 10 mm is specified to achieve a smooth finish and proper compaction.

q: 38. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
explain: As moisture evaporates from ordinary cement concrete after casting, the paste loses volume and the concrete undergoes drying shrinkage.

q: 39. The concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is essentially a composite material composed mainly of cement, sand, and aggregate (along with water), hence all of the above is correct.

q: 40. The impurity of mixing water which affects the setting time and strength of concrete, is
explain: Sodium carbonates and bicarbonates present in mixing water can adversely affect the setting time and reduce the strength of concrete.

q: 41. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete, is known
explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of solids.

q: 42. The fineness modulus of an aggregate is roughly proportional to
options: average size of the particles in the aggregate
explain: Fineness modulus is an empirical index that correlates roughly with the average particle size of the aggregate — a higher FM indicates coarser average particle size.

q: 43. The value of fineness modulus for fine sand may range between
explain: Per the classification used in this text, fine sand typically has a fineness modulus in the range of 2.2 to 2.6.

q: 44. Pick up the correct proportions of chemical ingredients of cement
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the typical approximate composition by percentage follows the order Lime : Silica : Alumina : Iron oxide as 63 : 22 : 6 : 3.

q: 45. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The degree of grinding of cement, is called fineness
The process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement.
The phenomenon by virtue to which cements does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement.
The heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as neat of hydration.
explain: This statement is incorrect: soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to resist volume expansion/change after setting, not to sound transmission — the two share a similar-sounding name but different meanings.

q: 46. Inert material of a cement concrete mix, is
explain: Aggregate serves as the chemically inert filler material in a concrete mix, while cement and water are the active binding agents that react with each other.

q: 47. If aggregates completely pass through a sieve of size 75 mm and are retained on sieve of size 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky is its minimum dimension is less than
explain: The mean dimension is the average of the two sieve sizes (75+60)/2 = 67.5mm; the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 of mean) gives 0.6 × 67.5 ≈ 40.5mm.

q: 48. Log angles machine is use to test the aggregate for
explain: The Los Angeles abrasion machine tests the aggregate's resistance to abrasion and impact by tumbling it with steel balls, primarily measuring abrasion resistance.

q: 49. The strength and quality of concrete, depends upon
explain: Aggregate grading, surface area, particle shape, and surface texture all influence the water demand, bond with cement paste, and packing density of concrete, so all of them collectively affect its strength and quality.

q: 50. The compressive strength of concrete determined from 150 mm × 150 mm cylinder as compared to that determined from 150 mm cube is
explain: Cylinder specimens generally record lower compressive strength than cube specimens of comparable size due to differences in the stress distribution and end-restraint effects during testing.
